name: Ristiklappi
description: Ristiklappi (Ristikontra variant) is a Finnish Sedma-group game for 4 in partnerships. Tricks won by last card of same rank as led. 5 cards each; stock. Point cards: A=11, 10=10, K=4, Q=3, J=2. 'Clean' rule: if team took a queen before stock empty, must later win a trick with a king (not won by queen) to clean. First to 7 game points wins.

history.origins: Ristiklappi originates in northern Finland and Lapland as a more elaborate variant of Ristikontra within the Sedma group of games, in which tricks are won by the last card of the same rank as led. The Sedma family is confined to a region from Lapland to Hungary. The game was popular in lumber camps and is documented as a Finnish point-trick game with the distinctive clean rule (queen-taking requiring a later king-trick).
timeline: 20th century: documented as Finnish Sedma variant in Lapland; related to Ristikontra.
history.cultural: Lumber camps and rural Lapland; played in fixed partnerships.
history.evolution: More elaborate than Ristikontra; adds the clean rule and 5-card hand.

rules.objective: 61+ card points; 'clean' if took queen in first part.
rules.gameplay: 1. Trick won by last card of same rank as led. 2. May play top stock card ('in the dark'). 3. Cannot lead same rank four tricks in a row. 4. Draw from stock after each trick. 5. Clean: if took queen before stock empty, must win trick with king (not by queen) in last 5 tricks. 6. Fail to clean = dishonourable loss.
